_description.summary: Autonomous and device-driven casting: Reverberation Rod loop control (delay, halt, reset, read/write rod memory), engines and gearboxes, Patterned Assembler and Spell Imprinter, Vessels, Pocket Simulator, Iotic Doors, dimension and spatial imprint queries, idea storage by key, Mediaweave collar, cellular automata and circles.
use_cases: Setting up or controlling rods, engines, assemblers, vessels or imprinters
Storing and retrieving values by key across casts (ideas, rod memory)
Querying dimensions, dimension height and scale, spatial imprints
Putting on or taking off Mediaweave

hexic:collar.d: Ties the mediaweave I am currently wearing. Costs a shard if it succeeds, or nothing if it didn't (I am either not wearing a mediaweave, or it is already tied).

hexic:connect.d: Casts the supplied Hex between each pair of elements in the given list, and splits the list at locations that return False.

hexic:decollar.d: Unties the mediaweave I am currently wearing. Costs a shard if it succeeds, or nothing if it didn't (I am either not wearing a mediaweave, or it is not tied).

hexic:dye_offpaw.d: Imbues the item held in my offhand (e.g. a casting item) with the given pigment.

hexic:engine/pos.d: Returns the position of the engine casting the current Hex. If any of these patterns are used outside a casting engine, mishaps rather spectacularly.

hexic:engine/sleep.d: Sleeps for at least the given number of seconds. Nature seems to round this to the next twentieth of a second.

hexic:engine/suspend.d: Suspends the current cast, as if I walked away from the engine (or stopped the rotor).

hexic:engine/terminate.d: Destroys the current cast, as if I stopped the rotor while sneaking. Any following patterns will never be cast.

hexic:erase.d: Erases the Hex or iota contained within a dropped item or block. Costs one dust per item.

hexic:extract.d: Extracts an iota from the given list, and breaks the list apart around it. Returns all items before the iota, all items after the iota, and finally the iota itself.

hexic:get_other_caster.d: Adds the closest sentient being, excluding me, to the stack.

hexic:grep.d: Discards iotas from the given list unless they satisfy the given predicate. Using Charon's Gambit discards the current and all remaining iotas.

hexic:mkmacro.d: Etches a macro into the given item entity with the given name (optional); removes a macro if the hex (topmost argument) is null. New macros cost 5 dust; replacing/removing macros is free.

hexic:modulo.d: Similar to Modulus, but differs for negative numbers: -8 %₁ 3 = -2, but -8 %₂ 3 = 1.

hexic:murmur.d: Adds the phrase on the *tip of my tongue* to the stack, regardless of whether I intend to say it.

hexic:reveal.d: Takes a list of iotas (or a single non-iota, which is treated as a list with one element) and embeds them in my mind persistently. Displayed iotas survive all methods that would clear a normal Reveal, and can only be cleared by another casting of Greater Reveal or my untimely demise.

hexic:staffcast_factory.d: Casts the given Hex as if from my staff, using its stack, etc. The Ravenmind (and perhaps other information) is carried across the boundary.

hexssence:extract_essence.d: Extracts the essence from a dropped item. Cost varies depending on target item.

hexssence:combine_essence.d: Remove a list of vectors, a recipe iota, and a vector from the stack, then take essences from the jars at the given locations, mix them according to the given recipe, and summon the resulting item at the given location.

hexssence:decay_recipe.d:
Decays a Recipe iota into a list of lists where the inner lists each contain an item type and a count.
This list of lists represents which essences the recipe needs, and how much of each.

oneironaut:getdim1.d: Returns a Spatial Imprint representing the dimension I am currently in. Costs a negligible amount of media.

oneironaut:getdim2.d: Returns a Spatial Imprint representing the dimension my sentinel is currently in. Costs one-tenth of an amethyst dust.

oneironaut:getdim/overworld.d: Returns a Spatial Imprint representing the overworld. Costs one-tenth of an amethyst dust.

oneironaut:getdim/nether.d:
Returns a Spatial Imprint representing the nether. Costs one-tenth of an amethyst dust.
There seems to be some resistance when I cast this. Perhaps I'll be able to overcome it with greater skill...

oneironaut:getdimheight.d: Accepts a Spatial Imprint, and returns the lowest and highest altitudes at which blocks can exist in the corresponding dimension.

oneironaut:getdimscale.d: Accepts a Spatial Imprint, and returns how many blocks you'd have to travel in the overworld to travel the equivalent of one block in the input dimension.

oneironaut:getrodlook.d: When cast with a Reverberation Rod, returns my look vector from when I started the current cast loop.

oneironaut:getrodpos.d: When cast with a Reverberation Rod, returns my eye position from when I started the current cast loop.

oneironaut:getrodstamp.d: When cast with a Reverberation Rod, returns the timestamp from when I started the current cast loop.

oneironaut:readrodram.d: Returns the iota stored in the current cast loop. Defaults to NULL.

oneironaut:writerodram.d: Accepts a non-list iota, and stores it inside the current cast loop. It will be lost when the cast loop ends.

oneironaut:readrodramremote.d: As Williams' Reflection, but can be cast from non-rod sources while a rod is in use.

oneironaut:writerodramremote.d: As Williams' Gambit, but can be cast from non-rod sources while a rod is in use.

oneironaut:readidea.d: Accepts a valid key, and returns the corresponding iota. Costs one-eigth of an amethyst dust.

oneironaut:readideatime.d: Accepts a valid key, and returns when the corresponding iota was inscribed, or -1. Costs no media.

oneironaut:readideawriter.d: Accepts a valid key and a player, and returns whether the corresponding iota was inscribed by that player. Costs no media.

oneironaut:readsentinel.d: Accepts a vector and a player, and returns either the distance from the vector to the target player's sentinel or NULL. Costs a negligible amount of media.

oneironaut:detectshroud.d: Accepts a vector and a number, and returns a list of unit vectors pointing from the initial vector to shrouded entities within a radius defined by the number.

oneironaut:delayrod.d: Accepts a positive integer. When cast with a Reverberation Rod, delays the current cast loop's next cast until that many twentieths of a second have passed.

oneironaut:haltrod.d: When cast with a Reverberation Rod, forcibly halts the current cast loop.

oneironaut:resetrod.d: Accepts a positive integer. Halts the current cast loop but also reduces the cooldown period from 1 second to ((1/20) \* number) seconds. Cooldown due to mishap is unaffected.

oneironaut:queryrod.d: Returns a boolean corresponding to whether the current cast is making use of a rod.

oneironaut:rodloopactive.d: Returns whether the caster is currently using a rod, regardless of the current cast is from that rod.

oneironaut:writeidea.d: Accepts a valid key and any iota, and stores it in the corresponding location. Costs a quarter of an amethyst dust.

oneironaut:craftrod.d: Acts just like the spells used to program conventional casting items. Costs 10 Charged Amethyst.

oneironaut:craftbottomlesstrinket.d: Writes a hex to the bottomless trinket in my other hand. Costs ten charged amethyst.

oneironaut:shiftsentinel.d: Accepts a spatial imprint, and moves my sentinel to its scaled coordinates in the corresponding dimension. Costs one amethyst shard. Mishaps if I do not currently have a sentinel.

slate_work:store_item.d: It is much easier to store an item into a Vessel than to pull it out. This pattern simply takes an Item Entity, and neatly sorts it into the activated Storage Vessels. Costs an 1/8th of a dust per activated Vessel.

slate_work:get_storage.d: This simply returns what Vessels the current Spell Circle has activated. I should likely use this to check if the Spell Circle has collected any Vessels.

slate_work:get_item.d: This takes a Hex and runs it on every Item Stack stored (with it on top of the stack). Once the Hex is executed, it requires a Integer, Vector, and Boolean, left on the stack, in that order.

slate_work:check_item.d: Check Item functions much like Reawaken Item; however, it only requires a Boolean from the inputted Hex. If the Boolean is ever True, the spell ends, and returns True.

slate_work:sort_items.d: In some rare scenarios, Vessels can get jumbled up and have items of the same type spread across different Vessels. This is a neat spell to resort them at a cost. That cost being 5 Charged Amethyst.

slate_work:set_craft.d: Sets the crafting recipe of a Patterned Assembler. Takes a list of Nulls, items, or item variants, and applies it to the targeted Assembler.

slate_work:get_craft_count.d: This gets how many times the Patterned Assembler will craft a recipe.

slate_work:set_craft_count.d: This sets how many times the Patterned Assembler will craft a recipe.

slate_work:set_macro.d:
This binds both a pattern and an iota to a Spell Imprinter, which is at the targeted vector. 
Does not mishap if casted outside of a Spell Circle. Costs a negligible amount of media.

slate_work:set_sents.d: This takes a list of vectors, and attempts to move the Pseudosentinels to the positions.

slate_work:get_sents.d: This retrieves the current positions of all Pseudosentinels in the order they were awoken. Free to cast.

slate_work:read_broadcast.d:
Attempts to read an Iotic Door at the given vector. If there is not a Door, returns garbage. 
Does not mishap if casted outside of a Spell Circle, free, and does not require ambit.

slate_work:set_slot.d: This takes a number between 0 and 5 (inclusive), and sets the held slot of the bound Pocket Simulator. Free.

slate_work:get_items.d: This returns all the items held within the Pocket Simulator as Item Stack Iotas. Free.

slate_work:get_trades.d: Despite the return of this spell, its not extremely complicated... I think. This takes a Merchant Directrix, and returns: [[Item Stack, Item Stack, Item Stack, Number]...]. Free to cast.

slate_work:exchange_mind.d: This feels... familiar. This spell takes a Villager, and a Merchant Directrix and exchanges their Jobs. Costs 1 Charged Amethyst to reapply the knowledge of Working.

slate_work:media_reflection.d: Adds the current amount of Media in the Impetus to the stack, in units of dust.
